explanation: A polar point is named by how FAR out it is (r) and which DIRECTION it points (theta). To get its everyday x,y address, drop a right triangle from the point: the horizontal leg is x = r·cos θ and the vertical leg is y = r·sin θ. Slide r to push the point in or out along its ray, and slide θ to swing the whole ray around — the dashed legs are exactly the x and y you read off.
bullets: r is the distance from the origin; θ is the direction (angle).
x = r·cos θ and y = r·sin θ are the two legs of a right triangle.
Negative r points the opposite way; θ can be given in degrees or radians.
